title: The AI Daily — Morning Conversation
blurb: An American-English dialogue limited to publisher feed excerpts.
lines: Hey, welcome to The AI Daily. I'm Maya, and Ben is here with me. We've picked a few headlines from publisher news feeds to talk through.
Hi, Maya. These are short feed excerpts, not the full articles, so we'll keep the facts carefully attributed and avoid filling in the blanks.
Let's start with Wired. The headline is: A New Breed of Chip Runs AI Models Using Waves of Light.
According to the publisher's excerpt, German company Q.ANT is trying to cut the amount of energy required to run AI models by using light to…
That brings us to TechCrunch Startups, which has this headline: Maple raises $5.3M to build AI products that protect your data, even from itself.
According to the publisher's excerpt, The startup's encrypted AI architecture is designed to prevent even the company itself from accessing users' private data.
Next up, The Decoder reports: Microsoft details how state-backed hackers use the ARTEX AI framework to automate cyberattacks.
According to the publisher's excerpt, Microsoft has published the technical architecture of ARTEX, an AI framework in wide use since July 2026 that runs cyberattacks…
And our fourth story is from TechCrunch AI: Nvidia hits pause on chip shipments to Southeast Asia.
According to the publisher's excerpt, Nvidia has told manufacturing partners to pause server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia as the U.S. tightens its…
Before we go, here's a useful expression: keep an eye on. It means watch something for changes — like a fast-moving AI story.
Exactly. And look into means investigate further. Follow the original reporting for context. See you in the next edition.
note: AI voices reading a conservative two-host script grounded only in publisher feed excerpts. Full article claims were not independently verified.
